newsitem.title: UK: Earth cooler last year, still warmer than average.
newsitem.headline: Earth cooler last year, still warmer than average.

text.p: The Earth was slightly cooler last year than in 1995 but still much warmer than the average, indicating that global warming is still taking place, British meteorologists said on Tuesday.
They said worldwide measurements showed the surface temperature of the Earth was about 0.21 degrees C (0.34 degree F) warmer than the average from 1961 to 1990.
"The warmest year, 1995, was 0.38 degrees C (0.68 degree F) warmer than this average," Britain's Meteorological Office said in a statement.
"Despite the reduced global warmth, 1996 remains consistent with the warming trend which began in the mid-1970s."

Climatologists say global warming does not mean consistently hotter temperatures the world over. It can cause more instability in the climate, meaning severe storms, droughts and freezes such as the one seen across Europe earlier this month.
The Meteorological Office and researchers at the University of East Anglia analysed data from more than 1,000 weather stations, ships, buoys, satellites and balloons.
